subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept outbound-staged generated HTML as trusted host-read input when a SQLite provenance row exists and sha256/size match the read buffer?
rationale: The source path and proof support the bug fix, but the PR intentionally expands a local HTML host-read security boundary beyond the temp root, which automation should not accept on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
options.body: Approve the SQLite sha256/size provenance lifecycle and land after exact-head CI stays green.

options.title: Require Tighter Lifecycle
options.body: Ask for additional bounds such as TTL/chunked cleanup or narrower owner hooks before accepting the expanded trust boundary.

options.title: Keep HTML Temp-Root Only
options.body: Decline this trust expansion and leave generated HTML delivery fail-closed after staging until a different owner-approved design exists.

recommendation.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
recommendation.body: Approve the SQLite sha256/size provenance lifecycle and land after exact-head CI stays green.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and has the clearest current history for accepting or rejecting the expanded lifecycle.
